def is_prime(n: int) -> bool:
    """Return whether n is prime.

    The function accepts non‑negative integers and implements a
    deterministic primality test based on trial division.  For the small
    numbers expected in the tests this is more than fast enough and has no
    external dependencies.

    If ``n`` is less than 2 it cannot be prime.  ``2`` is the only even
    prime; all other even numbers are composite.  For an odd ``n`` the
    algorithm checks divisibility by odd numbers up to ``sqrt(n)``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Non‑negative integer to test.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        ``True`` if ``n`` is prime, otherwise ``False``.
    """

    if n < 2:
        return False
    if n == 2:
        return True
    if n % 2 == 0:
        return False
    limit = int(n ** 0.5) + 1
    i = 3
    while i <= limit:
        if n % i == 0:
            return False
        i += 2
    return True
PY
